Assert that key columns identify each row uniquely

Source: R/expect_unique.R
expect_unique.Rd

A checkpoint for keys: every combination of the selected columns must occur at most once. On failure the duplicated rows are reported (and dumped, see expect_empty()) grouped by a dupid column, so each group of copies can be inspected together. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

expect_unique(
  data,
  ...,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL,
  log = getOption("expectr.log"),
  dump = getOption("expectr.dump")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

...

Key columns (tidy-select). If omitted, all columns are used, which checks for fully duplicated rows.

success_msg

Message shown (and logged) when data is empty. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the log names every check that ran, and "The dataset is empty." otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown (and logged) when duplicates exist and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description naming the key columns.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when data is not empty. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

log

Optional path to a log file. The directory is created automatically. Defaults to getOption("expectr.log").

dump

Optional directory. When the check fails, the offending rows are written there as a timestamped CSV file (UTF-8 with BOM, so Excel reads æøå correctly). Defaults to getOption("expectr.dump").

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

The most valuable place for it is just before a join. A lookup table with a duplicated key makes left_join() silently multiply rows; checking the key first turns that into an explicit message:

codes |>
  expect_unique(branche, abort_msg = "Codebook has duplicate codes") |>
  left_join(x = df, by = "branche")

This is flag_duplicates() + filter(isdup) + expect_empty() in one step, but faster: the full rows are only touched when there are duplicates to report.

See also

flag_duplicates(), expect_empty(), expect_none()

Examples

# Success: one row per model
dplyr::distinct(ggplot2::mpg, model) |>
  expect_unique(model)
#> ✔ Unique on model

# Warning: models appear in several years and variants
ggplot2::mpg |>
  expect_unique(model, year)
#> Warning: Duplicate rows on model, year
#> ℹ 227 rows in 69 groups:
#>     dupid model  year manufacturer displ   cyl trans     drv     cty   hwy fl
#>     <int> <chr> <int> <chr>        <dbl> <int> <chr>     <chr> <int> <int> <chr>
#>   1     1 a4     1999 audi           1.8     4 auto(l5)  f        18    29 p
#>   2     1 a4     1999 audi           1.8     4 manual(m… f        21    29 p
#>   3     1 a4     1999 audi           2.8     6 auto(l5)  f        16    26 p
#>   4     1 a4     1999 audi           2.8     6 manual(m… f        18    26 p
#>   5     2 a4     2008 audi           2       4 manual(m… f        20    31 p
#>   # ℹ 222 more rows
#>   # ℹ 1 more variable: class <chr>
#> ℹ Set `dump` or `options(expectr.dump = )` to write all rows to a CSV file.

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df |>
  expect_unique(cvr, year, abort_msg = "Duplicate company-years")
} # }
